choices: An interface that marks methods as deprecated
An empty interface used to tag a class as having some property
An interface with only default methods
An interface that extends multiple other interfaces
explanation: Marker interfaces have no methods — they exist purely to tag a class. Examples: java.io.Serializable (marks a class as serializable), java.lang.Cloneable (marks a class as cloneable). Modern Java often uses annotations instead of marker interfaces.
